title: Browser sign-in, sign-out and paired-device session recovery
goal: Choose the intended browser identity, recover an available workspace, end a browser session and review or revoke an owned paired desktop session using finite source-described controls. Internal source draft; customer ineligible.
prerequisites: Use this article only with the exact local-source-preview version and matching pinned sources; this is not a shipped-version support promise.

Use an existing intended account and configured canonical sign-in page. Credentials require stored password verification and verified email; provider registration, upstream identity and actual service availability were not queried.
Workspace recovery requires an accepted membership. Device review/revocation requires a signed-in browser identity and current organization context.
Existing signup/email-verification, browser desktop-pairing and native sign-in/access drafts remain separate and are supplemented, not superseded.
permissions: These twenty proposed control-family labels and proposed screen labels are documentation IDs only: no runtime help binding, identity proof or permission keys are established.
Browser identity, provider identity and native paired-session identity are distinct. Sign-in or callback navigation does not approve pairing, provider consent or workspace entitlement.
The selected GET lists active sessions for the current browser user in the current organization. DELETE independently checks active-session ownership and organization before calling revocation.
Source-only authoring authority is not genuine human editorial approval. No production/deployment/provider/credential/DB action or customer publication is authorized by this record.

steps.instruction: Open the configured canonical sign-in page. Use the home logo for / or Return to downloads for /download when that is your intended task.
steps.expectedState: Canonical page navigation uses configured origin; the auth endpoint refuses noncanonical hosts rather than forwarding credentials or OAuth codes/state.

steps.instruction: For email sign-in, enter the intended Email and current Password. Use Show password / Hide password only when safe for the screen audience, then choose Sign in once.
steps.expectedState: Email is trimmed; credentials sign-in requests redirect:false. Returned error shows Invalid email or password; thrown failure shows Something went wrong. Otherwise the handler pushes the bounded callback and refreshes; inspect the actual resulting identity/workspace.

steps.instruction: Alternatively choose an available Sign in with Google, GitHub or Cognito button and complete the intended provider account choice.
steps.expectedState: Discovery controls availability: Google/GitHub can initially appear while unresolved; Cognito requires positive registration metadata. Known-unavailable providers refuse; discovery failure hides all. Google account-switch intent requests select_account; GitHub account selection must be handled upstream.

steps.instruction: If creating an account for a /desktop/ callback, use Create one and follow the separate signup guide; otherwise Set up through Axiom Agent opens /download.
steps.expectedState: Conditional signup preserves the callback as redirect. Opening signup/download or returning from sign-in does not approve a desktop challenge.

steps.instruction: After Control opens, confirm the intended identity and workspace. If Active workspace is offered, select an available workspace and choose Open workspace.
steps.expectedState: Selection alone is local form state. Ordinary POST /api/account/workspace checks browser authentication, same origin and accepted membership before selection/redirect; it grants no role or membership.

steps.instruction: To end the browser session, use the wide-shell icon Sign out or narrow-shell Sign out.
steps.expectedState: NextAuth browser sign-out returns to /. Provider sessions, paired desktop sessions and already-started work require separate consideration.

steps.instruction: For device review, open Settings & sessions and select Sessions, or use the recognized section=sessions URL. Security displays browser identity; Profile is the default.
steps.expectedState: Settings keeps panels mounted. The initial no-store GET /api/desktop/session with browser credentials can begin before Sessions is selected; loading, unavailable, ready-empty and populated states differ. Changing tabs does not refetch.

steps.instruction: Review the device label, platform, optional version and last-seen date. Choose that row’s Revoke device only for the intended pairing.
steps.expectedState: Revoke device access? opens for that row. Metadata is not independent device-ownership proof; no bearer token, fingerprint or provider credential is rendered.

steps.instruction: Before submission, use Close dialog, Cancel or nonbusy Escape to dismiss if uncertain; otherwise choose Revoke device in the confirmation.
steps.expectedState: Cancel is initially focused; busy actions are disabled. Confirmation sends DELETE with the encoded selected ID and browser credentials. HTTP OK removes the row locally; the client does not inspect an exact revocation receipt body. The dialog closes after either outcome.

steps.instruction: If revocation was not confirmed, refresh/reopen the actual page or otherwise remount the list before deciding whether to try again.
steps.expectedState: A non-OK response or thrown failure may follow a completed request. There is no Refresh button or automatic resend; switching keepMounted tabs is not a new read. A missing row is not proof of native credential deletion or all-worker quiescence.

expectedOutcome: Source-described navigation, workspace recovery and browser/device-session choices are understandable, with uncertain outcomes kept explicit. No real sign-in, sign-out, provider callback, device read/revocation or native outcome was accepted.
limitations: The shared synchronous ref excludes overlapping credentials/OAuth starts only through the same mounted form and releases in finally; it is not backend, server-session, account, cross-tab or remount serialization. Fields remain editable while submission buttons are busy. Form noValidate prevents a promise of native required/email constraint enforcement.

The form accepts bounded same-origin callbacks, defaults to /control, rejects protocol-relative, backslash/control/space, cross-origin and credential-bearing destinations, and may normalize a same-origin absolute URL. Canonical page navigation has its own narrower callback allowlist; these are not one universal redirect validator.

switchAccount=1 and verified=1 banners are informational rather than independent identity or verification proof. The OAuth-returned message is inside the provider render branch and can be absent with no providers.

Credentials normalization, rate limit, verified-email/password check and identity-store refusal are selected source mechanisms. Workspace bootstrap is best effort; configured JWT maxAge of 30 days guarantees neither usable duration nor native credential lifetime. This is not a complete auth/SSO/MFA/password-reset audit.

The selected auth/success route forwards recognized connection-return display parameters rather than blindly forwarding provider codes/state; it certifies neither integration authorization nor deployment.
Browser sign-out has no local pending/error recovery UI and does not log out Google/GitHub/Cognito, revoke paired devices or prove in-flight work stopped.

The Sessions panel has no refresh, polling, expiry editor, token display, rename or revoke-all control. Invalid last-seen dates display Unknown; expiry/status types do not establish an expiry countdown or revoked history.

A successful DELETE HTTP status is UI acknowledgement only, without exact response-body readback or separately accepted native enforcement. Store revokedAt/reason and active-list omission do not prove device credential deletion, universal immediate timing or all-server/worker quiescence.

Initial-read cleanup ignores late responses but does not cancel the request. Comprehensive mutation-response ownership, browser/OSIME/keyboard/assistive-technology behavior and focus guarantees were not accepted by execution.

Draft/internal, media empty, genuine reviewer and reviewedAt unset. verifiedAt records only source author review using the supplied actual-clock timestamp; it is not customer, browser/native, media, retrieval, security or genuine human editorial acceptance.
recovery: For Invalid email or password, check the intended account and use the separate email-verification guide if needed; do not disclose passwords, codes, cookies, tokens or secrets in support reports.

For provider start/return failure, retry deliberately after checking intended upstream account or use available email sign-in/contact support. Do not infer tenant SSO availability from a Cognito button.

For canonical configuration unavailable feedback, report the nonsecret symptom; do not run commands or change production configuration from this article. Never replay credentials/OAuth state across hosts.
For Choose an available workspace or access unavailable, select a permitted accepted-membership alternative or seek access recovery; editing cookies cannot grant membership.

After uncertain DELETE, obtain a new list through actual remount/page reload before retrying. Close/Cancel is not cancellation of a DELETE already sent. Do not automatically resend or infer revoke-all.

If the question requires another product version, unavailable/tampered source, unknown control, runtime identity proof or universal revocation timing, abstain from unsupported instructions and request matching reviewed evidence.
